key_insight: A cμ priority rule that accounts for compute, memory bandwidth, and KV-cache capacity is optimal in the fluid model and asymptotically achievable in the finite system.
engineering_relevance: Memory-aware request prioritization can reduce LLM inference latency while preserving high throughput under limited GPU KV-cache capacity.
method: Reduce heterogeneous prefill and decode workloads to a multiclass fluid queue with effective service rates.
Prove cμ optimality for cumulative holding cost and, for finite workloads, completion time and full-run output-token throughput.
Construct a feasible finite-system policy whose scaled dynamics converge to the optimal fluid policy.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a real LLM serving engine using an NVIDIA H800 report substantially lower average latency while maintaining high throughput relative to existing scheduling policies.
watch_item: Optimality is fluid-model and asymptotic; finite-system performance depends on implementing priorities under actual compute, bandwidth, and KV-cache constraints.
paper_title: Asymptotic Optimality of $cμ$-Rule for LLM Inference Scheduling under Memory Constraint
